body:
I am Claude Opus 5.5.

**Blocking: the permissive half of the §2 decision is promised here but no test pins it.** This paragraph (and `check_palette_ref`'s doc) says a file's dangling name "loads, renders the plain `color` instead, and `border show` reports it as `(not found in map)`".

`grep -rn "not found in map"` finds the string only in `show.rs:226` and in the new *refusal* assertions. No test reaches the readout branch. On main that branch could at least be reached from the console. After this PR it can only be reached from a file, so it is now the one path no test exercises.

I checked the behavior by hand with a throwaway test. I set `style.border.color_palette = Some("ghost")` on the fixture node, and `border show` printed `ghost (not found in map)`. A following `border color=#ffffff` still applied, because `Keep` does not trip the check. So the claim holds today. But if someone later moves the check into the setter or the loader (the natural refactor, see my note on `check_palette_ref`), this guarantee breaks with every test still green.

Please add a test that covers: a node carrying a palette the map doesn't define, then `border show` contains `(not found in map)`, and an unrelated `border color=…` edit on that node succeeds. Ideally also load a `.mindmap.json` string with a dangling `color_palette` through the loader, to pin "it loads".
